title.desc: Ask in plain English. Deckhand asks for what it needs, runs the economics — NPV, breakeven and price sensitivity, plus a per-well and over-time value breakdown — and sends back a report you can keep.

turns.html: We're sizing up a subsea tieback and I want a quick read on whether it's worth sanctioning. Can you run the economics?

Happy to. A few numbers so I run it on your basis:
  • How many wells, and the production profile — peak rate and how it holds over the field life?
  • Up-front spend — host plus the subsea hardware per well (capex)?
  • Running cost — your operating cost per barrel (opex)?
  • Oil price to run it at, and the discount rate you sanction on?
If you've already rolled it up to an annual net cashflow, just send that — I'll work straight off it.
8-well subsea tieback. Profile rolls up to about $500M net a year for three years on $60/bbl, opex around $12/bbl. Capex is $1,000M up front. Discount at 10%. Annual cashflow is attached.

Got it — so I'll value $1,000M out, then $500M back each year for three years, discounted at 10%. From that I'll give you the NPV, the IRR and the payback, the breakeven oil price, and a per-well and year-by-year breakdown of where the value sits. Running it now…

Here's how the field stacks up at $60/bbl and a 10% discount:
MetricResultWhat it means
NPV$243.4MValue created after the 10% hurdle
IRR23.4%Well above the 10% sanction rate
Payback2.0 yrCapex back in two years
Worth sanctioning — it clears the 10% hurdle with $243M to spare and the return is more than double your cost of capital.
Before this goes to the sanction committee — what's our breakeven oil price, and which wells actually carry the field?

Breakeven is $44/bbl — about $16 of headroom under your $60 deck. NPV moves almost perfectly linearly with price, ≈ $15M for every $1/bbl:
Oil priceNPV @ 10%
$44 — breakeven~$0
$50$91M
$60 — your deck$243M
$70$395M
I've added two breakdowns to the report: a per-well NPV stackup (which wells carry the value once shared cost is allocated) and an over-time NPV bridge showing what moved value year by year — first oil, each completion.Same engine, real data: I run this on public BSEE records for 7 Gulf of Mexico Lower Tertiary fields — fully traceable, no black box.

report.title: Field Development Economics
report.inputs:
Field
Synthetic subsea tieback (illustrative) · 8 wells

Annual net cashflow ($M)
Year 0:  −1,000  (capex out)
Year 1:    +500
Year 2:    +500
Year 3:    +500

Basis
Oil price $60/bbl · Opex ≈ $12/bbl · Discount rate 10% · Annual periods
report.methodology:
1 · Roll the production profile, price and opex into a net cashflow for each year (capex sits in year 0).
2 · Discount every year back to today at 10%: PVᵢ = CFᵢ ÷ (1.10)ⁱ.
3 · NPV = Σ PVᵢ — the value left after the hurdle is paid.
4 · IRR = the discount rate that drives NPV to zero — the project's own rate of return.
5 · Payback = the year the running cash total first turns positive.
6 · Sanction test: NPV > 0 and IRR clears the 10% hurdle.
7 · Breakeven & price sensitivity: NPV is affine in the oil price, so one base run plus one scaled run pin the whole NPV-vs-price line and the breakeven (NPV = 0) — exact, not sampled.
8 · Decomposition: split the field NPV per well (production-pro-rata cost allocation) and year by year (the NPV bridge).
report.outputs:
MetricResultVerdict
NPV @ 10%$243.4M✅ Positive
IRR (annual)23.4%✅ Beats hurdle
Payback2.0 yr✅ Fast
Breakeven oil price$44/bbl✅ $16 headroom
Price sensitivity — NPV is linear in the oil price (≈ $15M per $1/bbl): $50 → $91M · $60 → $243M · $70 → $395M; breakeven at $44/bbl.

Where the value sits — a per-well NPV stackup (after shared-cost allocation) and a year-by-year NPV bridge (capex draw-down, first oil, each completion) accompany the headline number.

Verdict: WORTH SANCTIONING — clears the 10% hurdle with $243M to spare, IRR more than double the sanction rate, capex back inside two years, and $16/bbl of price headroom to breakeven.
Proven on real public data: the same engine runs 7 Gulf of Mexico Lower Tertiary fields from public BSEE OGOR-A + drilling records — fully traceable (worldenergydata/reports/lower_tertiary).
